title: 2020 AMC 10B Problem 19
statement: In a certain card game, a player is dealt a hand of \(10\) cards from a deck of \(52\) distinct cards. The number of distinct (unordered) hands that can be dealt to the player can be written as \(158A00A4AA0.\) What is the digit \(A?\)

solutions.text:
After canceling factors in the binomial coefficient, \[ \begin{aligned} \binom{52}{10} &=10\cdot17\cdot13\cdot7\\ &\quad\cdot47\cdot46\cdot11\cdot43. \end{aligned} \] Dividing \(158A00A4AA0\) by the final factor \(10,\) the units digit of the remaining product is \(A.\)

Working modulo \(10,\) \[ \begin{aligned} A&\equiv7\cdot3\cdot7\cdot7\cdot6\cdot1\cdot3\\ &\equiv2\pmod{10}. \end{aligned} \] Hence \(A=2.\) Thus, A is the correct answer.
hints: After factoring out a final \(10,\) only the units digit of the remaining product is needed
